$comment: The Gearbox ABI, machine-readable. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH.
Every language binding under sdk/ is a transcription of this file, and
tests/mod_abi_test.cpp asserts that the host's own function table matches it
exactly -- same modules, same names, same wire signatures, same capability.
So a binding written from this file cannot silently drift from the host: if
the host changes and this file does not, the build fails.
Wire types are WebAssembly value types. 'ptr' and 'len' are both i32; they
are called out separately only to document intent. A pointer is an offset
into your module's linear memory, which the host bounds-checks on every use.
Strings are (ptr, len) pairs of UTF-8 bytes. They are NOT null-terminated.
The host does not retain a pointer into your memory after a call returns.
VERSIONING. Every entry carries "since". 1.1 only APPENDS: no 1.0 name was
renamed, no signature changed, no function moved to a different capability,
so a mod written against 1.0 resolves every import it declares and behaves
exactly as it did. tests/mod_abi_test.cpp enforces that in both directions,
and the abi-compat CI step re-checks every 1.0 symbol against the committed
1.0 baseline so a future edit cannot quietly drop one.

modules.name: Core
modules.grants: Logging, environment introspection, abort, fuel budget

modules.name: GameState.Read
modules.grants: Read the turn, countries, treasuries, provinces

modules.name: UI
modules.grants: Register panels and draw inside them

modules.name: Assets
modules.grants: Read your own data/ directory

modules.name: GameProcess
modules.grants: Turn lifecycle hooks. Grants exports, not imports.

modules.name: GameState.Write
modules.grants: Mutate the world. Implies GameState.Read.

modules.name: Neural
modules.grants: Observe AI features and rewards (observe-only: no import writes to the model)

modules.name: Map
modules.grants: Province geometry and adjacency

modules.name: Diplomacy
modules.grants: Read and propose diplomatic actions

modules.name: Storage
modules.grants: Persistent key-value store namespaced to your mod id

modules.name: Audio
modules.grants: Play and stop sounds from your own mod's assets
modules.notes: Client-side only, and not because of trust: a server resolves turns and has nobody to play a sound to. A mod granted this on a server simply finds the calls do nothing.

modules.name: Net
modules.grants: Send and receive messages between copies of YOUR OWN mod
modules.notes: This is a channel between instances of one mod, NOT access to game traffic. A message is stamped by the host with the sending mod's id and the authenticated peer it came from, so a mod can neither read another mod's messages nor claim to be one. It cannot see or alter orders, turn deltas, tickets or chat -- those never pass through here. Raw packet access would let a client mod forge another player's orders, which is exactly what the server being authoritative exists to prevent. Delivery between machines is carried by the game, which lends the mod host a session while one exists; outside a network game every call answers 'not a network game', which is the right answer in singleplayer rather than an error.

modules.name: WasiStub
modules.grants: Minimal WASI shim so an interpreter-in-a-mod can boot. NOT a WASI implementation: no filesystem, deterministic randomness, no wall clock.

modules.name: Military.Read
modules.grants: Read ships, armies, fortifications and ports

modules.name: Military.Write
modules.grants: Queue army and ship orders through the turn resolver

modules.name: Research.Read
modules.grants: Read the technology tree and what each country has researched

modules.name: Research.Write
modules.grants: Set research funding

modules.name: Politics.Read
modules.grants: Read the political compass, policies, unrest and minorities

modules.name: Politics.Write
modules.grants: Enact and cancel policies through the game's own path

modules.name: Economy.Read
modules.grants: Read income, upkeep, industry and resources

modules.name: Economy.Write
modules.grants: Set province industry level

modules.name: MapEditor
modules.grants: Read and write the open map editor project; inert outside the editor

imports.name: log
imports.doc: Write a line to the game log and the mod menu's log view. Messages longer than 2048 bytes are truncated. An out-of-bounds (ptr,len) is refused and logged as an error against your mod rather than read.

imports.name: env
imports.doc: Fill a gearbox_env_t. Write your own sizeof into out->size FIRST; the host writes at most that many bytes, so an older mod stays safe against a newer host. If size is 0 or larger than the host's struct, the host uses its own size.

imports.name: abort
imports.doc: Unrecoverable error. Traps out of the current call, disables the mod, and shows the message to the user. Prefer returning an error from a hook where you can.

imports.name: fuel_budget
imports.doc: The instruction budget for the current hook, or 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF when unmetered. This is the LIMIT, not a live countdown: it does not decrease as you run. Use it to size your work up front and count your own iterations.

imports.name: turn_number
imports.doc: The current turn. 0 when no world is loaded.

imports.name: country_count
imports.doc: How many countries exist. 0 when no world is loaded. Rebel factions are not included.

imports.name: country_at
imports.doc: The country at index in [0, country_count). Returns GEARBOX_INVALID (0xFFFFFFFF) if out of range. Ordering is stable within a turn but not across turns.

imports.name: country_name
imports.doc: Two-call sizing. Writes at most cap bytes of UTF-8 and returns the FULL length. Call with cap 0 to size, then again to fill. A return greater than cap means truncation, not failure. Returns 0 for an unknown country.

imports.name: country_treasury
imports.doc: Treasury balance. 0 for an unknown country.

imports.name: country_province_count
imports.doc: How many provinces the country owns. 0 for an unknown country.

imports.name: province_population
imports.doc: Population of a province. 0 for an unknown province.

imports.name: province_owner
imports.doc: Owning country, or GEARBOX_INVALID if unowned or unknown.

imports.name: panel_register
imports.doc: Register a panel and return its handle. Returns 0 (invalid) when headless, when UI was revoked, or when you already hold 8 panels. Titles are truncated to 64 bytes. Call this from mod_load, not from your draw hook.

imports.name: draw_rect
imports.doc: Filled rectangle in panel-relative coordinates. Colour is 0xRRGGBBAA. Coordinates outside the panel are clipped by the host; they cannot escape it.

imports.name: draw_text
imports.doc: UTF-8 text in panel-relative coordinates. Truncated to 512 bytes per call.

imports.name: button
imports.doc: Immediate-mode button: draws it and returns 1 on the frame it is clicked. One click activates one button -- the host consumes it, so overlapping rects do not all fire. Label truncated to 64 bytes.

imports.name: size
imports.doc: Byte size of one of your own data/ files, or 0 if there is no such asset. Names are relative to data/ and use '/' separators: data/flags/fr.png is "flags/fr.png".

imports.name: read
imports.doc: Two-call sizing, like country_name. Writes at most cap bytes and returns the asset's full size. The name is looked up in your package's entry list, never resolved as a filesystem path.

imports.name: play
imports.doc: Play a sound from your own mod's assets. `path` is relative to your mod root; a path outside it is refused rather than resolved. Volume is 0..1 and is multiplied by the player's own effects setting, so a mod cannot be louder than they allowed. Returns a handle, or 0 if it could not be played.

imports.name: stop
imports.doc: Stop a sound this mod started. A handle belonging to another mod, or one that already finished, does nothing.

imports.name: set_volume
imports.doc: Change the volume of a playing sound, 0..1, again scaled by the player's setting.

imports.name: is_playing
imports.doc: Whether that handle is still making sound.

imports.name: send
imports.doc: Send a message to the same mod running on another peer. `peer` is a peer id -- the value `recv` reported in `from_peer` -- and -1 broadcasts to every other peer, the host included. There is no fixed id for the host: a host that plays holds an ordinary seat, and a dedicated one holds none. The host stamps your mod id on the message, so you cannot send as another mod, and it never carries game traffic: orders, deltas and chat do not travel here. Messages larger than 8192 bytes are refused. Returns 0 if this is not a network game, or the message was too large.

imports.name: recv
imports.doc: Take the next message addressed to this mod, writing it into `out` and the sender's peer id into `from_peer`. Returns the number of bytes written, or 0 when the queue is empty. A message longer than `out_len` is truncated rather than dropped, so a small buffer loses data instead of stalling the queue.

imports.name: peer_count
imports.doc: How many players this session has, a playing host included. 0 when this is not a network game, which is how a mod tells the difference. Spectators are not counted.

imports.name: self_peer
imports.doc: This machine's own peer id. 0 means this is not a network game, or this is a dedicated host holding no seat -- a host that plays has an ordinary peer id like anyone else, so do not use this to tell host from client. `is_host` is that question.

imports.name: is_host
imports.doc: Whether this copy is the authoritative one. A mod that computes anything the game depends on must do it here and send the result, not compute it separately on each machine.

imports.name: fd_write
imports.doc: Writes to fd 1 or 2 only, and the bytes go to the mod log where the user can see them. Any other fd returns EBADF. This is how print() in an interpreted mod reaches you.

imports.name: proc_exit
imports.doc: Traps the mod. A runtime calling exit() must not return into code that believes the process is gone.

imports.name: random_get
imports.doc: DETERMINISTIC pseudo-random bytes, seeded from your mod id -- not OS entropy. Real entropy is a machine fingerprint and would make self-play and save replay irreproducible. Two mods get different streams; one mod gets the same stream every run. Do not use for anything security-relevant.

imports.name: clock_time_get
imports.doc: Returns the turn number expressed as nanoseconds, not the wall clock. Monotonic and coarse. A mod cannot learn the real date, the timezone, or how long anything took -- all of which are fingerprints.

imports.name: environ_sizes_get
imports.doc: Always reports zero variables. There is no environment.

imports.name: environ_get
imports.doc: No-op; there is no environment to write.

imports.name: args_sizes_get
imports.doc: Always reports zero arguments. Reports success rather than failing, because runtimes commonly abort at startup if argv cannot be read.

imports.name: args_get
imports.doc: No-op; there are no arguments.

imports.name: fd_close
imports.doc: EBADF. There are no real descriptors.

imports.name: fd_fdstat_get
imports.doc: ENOTCAPABLE.

imports.name: fd_prestat_get
imports.doc: ENOTCAPABLE. No preopened directories, so no filesystem root exists to walk.

imports.name: fd_prestat_dir_name
imports.doc: ENOTCAPABLE.

imports.name: fd_read
imports.doc: ENOTCAPABLE. There is no stdin and no file to read.

imports.name: fd_seek
imports.doc: EBADF.

imports.name: path_open
imports.doc: ENOTCAPABLE, always. Opening a file is refused rather than stubbed -- this is the single import that would turn the shim into the hole the sandbox exists to prevent.

imports.name: clock_res_get
imports.doc: Reports a fixed, coarse resolution matching clock_time_get's one-tick-per-turn granularity. Claiming anything finer would be a lie a runtime might act on.

imports.name: sched_yield
imports.doc: Succeeds and does nothing. A mod is single-threaded; there is nothing to yield to.

imports.name: fd_advise
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). There is no filesystem.

imports.name: fd_allocate
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). There is no filesystem.

imports.name: fd_datasync
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). There is no filesystem.

imports.name: fd_sync
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). There is no filesystem.

imports.name: fd_fdstat_set_flags
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). There is no filesystem.

imports.name: fd_filestat_get
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). File metadata would describe a filesystem the mod cannot reach.

imports.name: fd_tell
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). There is no filesystem.

imports.name: fd_renumber
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). There are no descriptors to renumber.

imports.name: fd_filestat_set_size
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). There is no filesystem.

imports.name: fd_filestat_set_times
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). There is no filesystem.

imports.name: fd_pread
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). Reading is not provided; assets come from the Assets module instead.

imports.name: fd_pwrite
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). A mod cannot write files; use the host log.

imports.name: fd_readdir
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). Listing a directory would reveal a filesystem the sandbox denies.

imports.name: path_create_directory
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). There is no filesystem, by design.

imports.name: path_remove_directory
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). There is no filesystem, by design.

imports.name: path_unlink_file
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). There is no filesystem, by design.

imports.name: path_filestat_get
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). Answering would tell a mod whether a path exists on your machine.

imports.name: path_symlink
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). There is no filesystem, by design.

imports.name: path_readlink
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). There is no filesystem, by design.

imports.name: path_rename
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). There is no filesystem, by design.

imports.name: path_link
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). There is no filesystem, by design.

imports.name: path_filestat_set_times
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). There is no filesystem, by design.

imports.name: poll_oneoff
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). There is nothing to poll: no files, no sockets, no timers a mod may wait on.

imports.name: sock_accept
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). A mod has no network access, which is much of the point of the sandbox.

imports.name: sock_recv
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). A mod has no network access.

imports.name: sock_send
imports.doc: Refused (ENOTCAPABLE). A mod has no network access.

imports.name: sock_shutdown
imports.doc: Refused (EBADF). A mod has no network access.

imports.name: get
imports.doc: Reads one of your own keys. Two-call sizing: returns the full value length and writes at most cap bytes. Returns GEARBOX_INVALID if the key is absent -- which is NOT the same as a zero-length value, so you can tell 'never stored' from 'stored empty'. Values are arbitrary bytes, not text.

imports.name: set
imports.doc: Stores bytes under one of your own keys. Returns 1 on success, 0 if a quota was exceeded (256 keys, 128-byte keys, 16 KiB per value, 64 KiB total per mod) -- the reason is written to your log. Not written to disk immediately: the store is flushed at turn boundaries and on unload, because a mod may call this from a draw hook.

imports.name: remove
imports.doc: Deletes one of your own keys. Returns 1 if it existed, 0 if it did not.

imports.name: width
imports.doc: Width of the province map in pixels. 0 when no world is loaded.

imports.name: height
imports.doc: Height of the province map in pixels. 0 when no world is loaded.

imports.name: province_count
imports.doc: How many provinces the loaded map has. 0 when no world is loaded.

imports.name: province_at
imports.doc: Province handle at an index in [0, province_count). Returns GEARBOX_INVALID if out of range. The order is stable across runs, unlike the game's internal storage, so an index is safe to remember within a session.

imports.name: province_name
imports.doc: The province's name. Two-call sizing: returns the full length and writes at most cap bytes. Empty for an unknown province.

imports.name: province_center_x
imports.doc: X pixel coordinate of the province's centre. 0 for an unknown province.

imports.name: province_center_y
imports.doc: Y pixel coordinate of the province's centre. 0 for an unknown province.

imports.name: province_is_land
imports.doc: 1 if the province is land, 0 if it is sea or unknown. Sampled at the province centre.

imports.name: province_neighbor_count
imports.doc: How many provinces border this one. 0 for an unknown province.

imports.name: province_neighbor_at
imports.doc: The bordering province at an index in [0, province_neighbor_count). GEARBOX_INVALID if out of range. Adjacency is computed once when the map loads, so walking it is cheap.

imports.name: at_war
imports.doc: 1 if the two countries are at war. Relations are symmetric, so the argument order does not matter. 0 for unknown countries or for a country with itself.

imports.name: allied
imports.doc: 1 if the two countries are allied.

imports.name: non_aggression
imports.doc: 1 if the two countries have a non-aggression pact.

imports.name: guaranteed
imports.doc: 1 if the first country guarantees the second.

imports.name: propose_war
imports.doc: PROPOSES a declaration of war, and returns 1 only if the game accepted it. It is routed through the same code path any other actor uses, so guarantee chains and war consequences follow exactly as normal -- a mod cannot produce a diplomatic state the game itself could not reach. Refused (0) if either country is unknown, they are the same country, or they are already at war. Either outcome is written to your mod log, so a player can see after the fact that a mod started a war.

imports.name: set_country_treasury
imports.doc: Sets a country's treasury outright. Returns 1 on success, 0 if the country is unknown or the value is not finite and within +/-1e12 -- NaN or infinity would silently poison every later calculation, so they are refused rather than stored.

imports.name: add_country_treasury
imports.doc: Adds to a country's treasury. Usually what you want instead of set: it composes with whatever the economy did this turn. Refused (0) if the result would leave the sane range.

imports.name: set_province_owner
imports.doc: Transfers a province to another country. Routed through the same code the game's own ceasefires use, so the province, the ownership lookup, the per-pixel country map and both countries' pixel lists all stay consistent -- and the previous owner's troops in that province are disbanded, as they are for any other transfer. Returns 0 if either handle is unknown or the country already owns it. Always written to your mod log: territory changing hands is the most consequential thing a mod can do.

imports.name: feature_count
imports.doc: How many floats are in the AI's feature vector. 0 when there is no AI or no world.

imports.name: features
imports.doc: Copies the feature vector the AI would see for a country, as 32-bit floats. Two-call sizing, but note cap counts FLOATS and the buffer must therefore be cap*4 bytes. This is a snapshot: writing to your copy does not affect the AI.

imports.name: reward_count
imports.doc: How many reward channels the AI tracks (economy, politics, war, navy).

imports.name: reward_mean
imports.doc: The running mean reward for one channel, indexed in [0, reward_count). 0 if out of range. OBSERVE ONLY: this capability has no import that writes to the model, the optimiser state or the reward history, which is deliberate -- a trained model is hours of work and a mod that could quietly retrain it is not something a user can meaningfully consent to.

imports.name: set_province_population
imports.doc: Sets a province's population. Returns 0 if the province is unknown, the value is negative, or it exceeds 100 billion. The game stores population in two places -- a map and a dense array used by the population texture -- and this updates both, which is why it exists as an import rather than being something a mod could do by other means.

imports.name: draw_line
imports.doc: Queue a line from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2) in panel-relative pixels. Thickness is clamped to 0.25..64. Clipped to your panel like every other command.

imports.name: draw_circle
imports.doc: Queue a filled circle centred at (cx,cy), panel-relative. Radius is clamped to 0..4096.

imports.name: draw_image
imports.doc: Queue an image from YOUR OWN package -- `name` is a path inside your .odmod, resolved exactly as gearbox:assets/read resolves it, so you cannot name a file on disk, a game asset, or another mod's art. Pass w or h as 0 to use the image's own size. tint 0xFFFFFFFF draws it unmodified. Decoded once and cached; a name that fails to decode draws nothing and does not retry. PNG, JPG, BMP, TGA and GIF are recognised by extension. This is the call that makes a real reskin possible.

imports.name: draw_text_sized
imports.doc: Like draw_text but with a type size, clamped to 6..96. draw_text remains 14pt, unchanged, so v1.0 mods look exactly as they did.

imports.name: measure_text
imports.doc: Width in pixels of `text` at `size`, measured with the font the game will actually draw. Centring, right-alignment and wrapping all need this before the text is queued.

imports.name: panel_width
imports.doc: The width the host assigned your panel this frame, in pixels. Lay out against this rather than against min_w -- the host may have given you more.

imports.name: panel_height
imports.doc: The height the host assigned your panel this frame, in pixels.

imports.name: panel_set_visible
imports.doc: Show or hide one of your panels. A hidden panel is not drawn and receives no input, but keeps its handle and its registration.

imports.name: mouse_x
imports.doc: Cursor X, panel-relative, or 0 when the cursor is not over your panel. You cannot observe the pointer outside your own box.

imports.name: mouse_y
imports.doc: Cursor Y, panel-relative, or 0 when the cursor is not over your panel.

imports.name: mouse_inside
imports.doc: Whether the cursor is over your panel this frame.

imports.name: theme_accent
imports.doc: The PLAYER's accent colour as 0x00RRGGBB -- not another mod's override. Build your palette around this and you harmonise with what they chose.

imports.name: set_theme_accent
imports.doc: Restyle the whole interface. The accent is read at over a hundred sites -- every heading, highlight, selection and button -- so this is the cheapest full reskin there is. It is NOT persisted: the game's settings file keeps the player's own colour, and the override is dropped the moment no mod is running, so it cannot outlive uninstalling you.

imports.name: ship_count
imports.doc: How many ships exist in the world, across all owners.

imports.name: ship_at
imports.doc: The ship id at `index` in 0..ship_count-1, or 0xFFFFFFFF past the end. Ids are stable within a turn and not across turns -- do not store one.

imports.name: ship_exists
imports.doc: Whether a ship id is still live. Check this before acting on an id you read earlier in the same turn; ships sink.

imports.name: ship_owner
imports.doc: The country that owns a ship, or 0xFFFFFFFF for an id that does not exist.

imports.name: ship_type
imports.doc: The hull type as a lowercase string: "transport", "destroyer", "battleship", "carrier", "submarine". Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: ship_lon
imports.doc: Longitude in degrees, -180..180. Ships live in world coordinates, not provinces.

imports.name: ship_lat
imports.doc: Latitude in degrees, -90..90.

imports.name: ship_health
imports.doc: Hull integrity, 0..100. A ship at 0 has already sunk and will not appear.

imports.name: ship_crew
imports.doc: Crew aboard. For a transport this includes the embarked army, which is why a sunk transport costs so much more than its hull.

imports.name: ship_range
imports.doc: How far this hull may move in one turn, in degrees. The resolver clamps any order beyond it, so read this before ordering a move rather than discovering the clamp afterwards.

imports.name: army_stack_count
imports.doc: How many distinct owners have troops in a province. Usually 1; more than one means a contested or garrisoned province.

imports.name: army_stack_owner
imports.doc: The country owning stack `index` in a province, or 0xFFFFFFFF past the end.

imports.name: army_stack_size
imports.doc: How many troops are in that stack.

imports.name: country_army
imports.doc: A country's total troops everywhere, which is the number its own army screen shows.

imports.name: province_fortification
imports.doc: Fortification level, 0..5. Multiplies the defender's strength.

imports.name: province_port_level
imports.doc: Port level, 0..3. 0 means no port, so no embarking and no ship repair.

imports.name: order_army_move
imports.doc: Move `percent` (0..100) of the troops in `from` into the adjacent province `to`. Into an enemy province this is an attack; into your own or an ally's it is a transfer. Non-adjacent moves are refused. QUEUES AN ORDER; it does not move anything. It lands in the same queue the player's own click writes to and is validated by the same resolver at end of turn, so a mod cannot teleport, cheat range, or attack across an ocean. Returns 0 if the order is rejected outright.

imports.name: order_ship_move
imports.doc: Sail a ship toward (lon,lat). The resolver routes around land and clamps to ship_range, so a destination on land or beyond range moves the ship as far as it legally can rather than failing. QUEUES AN ORDER; it does not move anything. It lands in the same queue the player's own click writes to and is validated by the same resolver at end of turn, so a mod cannot teleport, cheat range, or attack across an ocean. Returns 0 if the order is rejected outright.

imports.name: order_ship_engage
imports.doc: Attack another ship. Requires that you are at war with its owner and that it is within range; both are checked by the resolver. QUEUES AN ORDER; it does not move anything. It lands in the same queue the player's own click writes to and is validated by the same resolver at end of turn, so a mod cannot teleport, cheat range, or attack across an ocean. Returns 0 if the order is rejected outright.

imports.name: order_ship_bombard
imports.doc: Bombard a coastal province. `ammo` names the shell type; pass an empty string for the default. QUEUES AN ORDER; it does not move anything. It lands in the same queue the player's own click writes to and is validated by the same resolver at end of turn, so a mod cannot teleport, cheat range, or attack across an ocean. Returns 0 if the order is rejected outright.

imports.name: node_count
imports.doc: How many technologies exist in the tree.

imports.name: node_id
imports.doc: The stable string id of technology `index`, which is what country_has_researched takes. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: node_name
imports.doc: The technology's display name, which is localised and NOT stable -- never match on it. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: node_category
imports.doc: Which branch of the tree it sits in. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: node_cost
imports.doc: Research points required.

imports.name: country_has_researched
imports.doc: Whether a country has completed a technology. Takes the id from node_id, not the display name.

imports.name: country_funding
imports.doc: Research funding as A SHARE OF INCOME, 0..1 -- not an absolute sum. That is how the game stores it and how its own economy screen presents it.

imports.name: set_country_funding
imports.doc: Set research funding as a share of income. Clamped to 0..1; a value in 'points per turn' is not a quantity this game has.

imports.name: country_compass_econ
imports.doc: Economic axis of the political compass, -100 (planned) to 100 (market).

imports.name: country_compass_social
imports.doc: Social axis, -100 (authoritarian) to 100 (libertarian).

imports.name: province_unrest
imports.doc: This province's chance of rebelling, as the game itself computes it.

imports.name: policy_count
imports.doc: How many policies exist.

imports.name: policy_id
imports.doc: The stable string id of policy `index`. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: policy_name
imports.doc: The policy's display name; localised, not stable, do not match on it. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: country_has_policy
imports.doc: Whether a country currently has a policy active or implementing.

imports.name: province_minority_count
imports.doc: How many named minority groups live in a province.

imports.name: province_minority_name
imports.doc: The minority's name. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: province_minority_share
imports.doc: That minority's share of the province's population, 0..1.

imports.name: set_country_policy
imports.doc: Enact or cancel a policy. GOES THROUGH THE GAME'S OWN enactPolicy, so the cost, the prerequisites and the per-turn enactment cap all still apply -- a country cannot end up running policies it could never have afforded. Returns 1 if the policy is already in the requested state.

imports.name: country_income_gross
imports.doc: Income per turn before upkeep.

imports.name: country_income_net
imports.doc: Income per turn after army and navy upkeep. Negative means the treasury is draining.

imports.name: country_army_upkeep
imports.doc: What the standing army costs per turn.

imports.name: country_navy_upkeep
imports.doc: What the fleet costs per turn. Ships a country is not using still cost this, which is what makes scrapping a real decision.

imports.name: country_is_bankrupt
imports.doc: Whether a country is currently bankrupt.

imports.name: province_industry_level
imports.doc: Industry level, 0..10.

imports.name: province_industry_specialization
imports.doc: What this province's industry specialises in, or an empty string for none. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: province_resource
imports.doc: How much of a resource a province holds, 0..100. `which` is one of "oil", "gold", "rubber", "gemstones", "metal"; anything else reads 0.

imports.name: set_province_industry_level
imports.doc: Set a province's industry level, clamped to 0..10. This writes the built level directly and does not charge for it -- it is a scenario-authoring tool, not a build order.

imports.name: province_is_coastal
imports.doc: Whether a province touches water. Ports, embarking and naval bombardment all require it.

imports.name: sea_route_exists
imports.doc: Whether a fleet could get from one point to another by sea, using the game's own navigation grid. You cannot compute this from province neighbours: those describe LAND adjacency.

imports.name: point_is_land
imports.doc: Whether a world coordinate is land. Ordering a ship onto land is not an error -- the resolver clamps it -- but knowing first is cheaper.

imports.name: editor_active
imports.doc: Whether the map editor is open with a project loaded. EVERY OTHER CALL IN THIS MODULE returns 0 or an empty string when this is 0, including from inside a running game: the data behind them is an editor project, and a game does not have one. Check this first.

imports.name: editor_province_count
imports.doc: How many provinces the open project has. Returns a neutral value unless the map editor is open with a project loaded -- see mapeditor/active.

imports.name: editor_province_at
imports.doc: The province id at `index`, in ascending id order, or 0xFFFFFFFF past the end. Returns a neutral value unless the map editor is open with a project loaded -- see mapeditor/active.

imports.name: editor_province_population
imports.doc: Population. Returns a neutral value unless the map editor is open with a project loaded -- see mapeditor/active.

imports.name: editor_province_industry_level
imports.doc: Industry level, 0..10. Returns a neutral value unless the map editor is open with a project loaded -- see mapeditor/active.

imports.name: editor_province_fortification
imports.doc: Fortification, 0..5. Returns a neutral value unless the map editor is open with a project loaded -- see mapeditor/active.

imports.name: editor_province_port_level
imports.doc: Port level, 0..3. Returns a neutral value unless the map editor is open with a project loaded -- see mapeditor/active.

imports.name: editor_province_resource
imports.doc: Resource amount, 0..100. `which` is "oil", "gold", "rubber", "gemstones" or "metal". Returns a neutral value unless the map editor is open with a project loaded -- see mapeditor/active.

imports.name: editor_province_compass_econ
imports.doc: Province economic compass, -100..100. Returns a neutral value unless the map editor is open with a project loaded -- see mapeditor/active.

imports.name: editor_province_compass_social
imports.doc: Province social compass, -100..100. Returns a neutral value unless the map editor is open with a project loaded -- see mapeditor/active.

imports.name: editor_set_province_population
imports.doc: Set population, clamped to 0..2e9. Writes the SAME per-province data the editor's own tools write, so it saves, exports and shows up in the unsaved-changes prompt like any other edit. A province the project does not have is refused rather than created: data without a shape on the province bitmap exports a map the game cannot load.

imports.name: editor_set_province_industry_level
imports.doc: Set industry level, clamped to 0..10. Writes the SAME per-province data the editor's own tools write, so it saves, exports and shows up in the unsaved-changes prompt like any other edit. A province the project does not have is refused rather than created: data without a shape on the province bitmap exports a map the game cannot load.

imports.name: editor_set_province_fortification
imports.doc: Set fortification, clamped to 0..5. Writes the SAME per-province data the editor's own tools write, so it saves, exports and shows up in the unsaved-changes prompt like any other edit. A province the project does not have is refused rather than created: data without a shape on the province bitmap exports a map the game cannot load.

imports.name: editor_set_province_port_level
imports.doc: Set port level, clamped to 0..3. Writes the SAME per-province data the editor's own tools write, so it saves, exports and shows up in the unsaved-changes prompt like any other edit. A province the project does not have is refused rather than created: data without a shape on the province bitmap exports a map the game cannot load.

imports.name: editor_set_province_resource
imports.doc: Set a resource amount, clamped to 0..100. An unrecognised name is refused rather than silently mapped onto oil. Writes the SAME per-province data the editor's own tools write, so it saves, exports and shows up in the unsaved-changes prompt like any other edit. A province the project does not have is refused rather than created: data without a shape on the province bitmap exports a map the game cannot load.

imports.name: editor_set_province_compass
imports.doc: Set both compass axes, each clamped to -100..100. Writes the SAME per-province data the editor's own tools write, so it saves, exports and shows up in the unsaved-changes prompt like any other edit. A province the project does not have is refused rather than created: data without a shape on the province bitmap exports a map the game cannot load.

imports.name: editor_map_name
imports.doc: The project's map name. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: editor_set_map_name
imports.doc: Rename the map. Refused if empty or over 96 bytes.

imports.name: editor_set_author
imports.doc: Set the author recorded in the exported .odmap. Up to 96 bytes.

imports.name: editor_set_license
imports.doc: Set the licence recorded in the exported .odmap. Up to 96 bytes.

imports.name: peer_at
imports.doc: The peer id at `index` in 0..peer_count-1, or 0xFFFFFFFF past the end. This is the id net/send takes.

imports.name: peer_name
imports.doc: That peer's display name -- deliberately NOT their account id or issuer. A mod has no business correlating players across sessions. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: max_message_bytes
imports.doc: The largest payload net/send will accept. Chunk against this rather than discovering the limit by having a message dropped.

imports.name: module_count
imports.doc: How many decision modules the AI has. Each acts independently every turn.

imports.name: module_name
imports.doc: The module's name: "economy", "politics", "war", "navy". Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: action_count
imports.doc: How many actions that module can choose between.

imports.name: action_name
imports.doc: The action's name, e.g. "reinforce", "embark", "propose_alliance". THE FEATURE VECTOR IS DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED: its 143 slots are an implementation detail that has changed before and will again, and a mod written against those names would break silently. What the AI CAN DO is stable enough to build an advisor or a decision log against. Two-call sizing: call with cap 0 to learn the length, allocate, call again. Returns the full length either way; the copy is truncated to cap.

imports.name: country_is_ai
imports.doc: Whether a country is played by the AI rather than by the local player.

imports.name: update_count
imports.doc: Gradient updates the loaded model has been through -- roughly, how much training it has seen.

imports.name: model_loaded
imports.doc: Whether an AI model is loaded at all. False in a game with no AI players.

exports.name: mod_load
exports.doc: Called once when your mod is enabled, before anything else. Return 0 to accept the load; non-zero refuses it and the value is shown to the user. There is no autorun, so this runs every session the user enables you -- never assume prior state.

exports.name: mod_unload
exports.doc: Called when disabled, reloaded, or at shutdown. Release what you hold. Your state does not survive a reload and there is no hook to serialise it.

exports.name: mod_pre_turn
exports.doc: Called before the host processes a turn. Only invoked if GameProcess is granted.

exports.name: mod_post_turn
exports.doc: Called after the host processes a turn. Only invoked if GameProcess is granted.

exports.name: mod_draw_panel
exports.doc: Called once per frame per visible panel you registered. Never called when headless. Re-issue all your draw calls every frame; the command list is cleared between frames.

env_struct.$comment: Layout is ABI. Fields are only ever appended, never reordered or resized. Total size is 28 bytes on wasm32.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: You write sizeof(gearbox_env_t) here before calling env

fields.name: is_web
fields.doc: 1 under Emscripten. Fuel is NOT enforced there.

fields.name: is_headless
fields.doc: 1 when there is no renderer. UI imports no-op.

fields.name: net_role
fields.doc: enum:net_role. 0 in singleplayer, which is what an older mod reading this byte as reserved already saw.
